title: Card population registry v1
description: WHICH CARDS A COMPILER MAY READ, AND FOR WHAT. Authored by 0.4.0_DT_ClientPlatform~X to 4.0.0_SA_CRO~A's admission ruling, reworked to their release-gate FAIL. It exists because a GLOB WAS BEING USED AS AN AUTHORITY BOUNDARY: the discovery pattern had a wave number baked into it, so the compiler's honest '0 exact matches' was a true statement about its own configuration that every reader took as a statement about the estate (doctrine principle 13). A registry moves admission from a pattern that silently changes meaning each wave to an ENUMERATION that can only change by being edited. PLACED IN THE COMPILER'S OWN DELIVERABLE DIRECTORY, NOT org/standards/: this is a lane artifact proposed for promotion, and promoting it is 4.0.0_SA_CRO~A's act.

registry_version.description: Pinned. A consumer branches on this before reading anything else, and the v1 clauses at the bottom of this file bind only while it reads v1.

ratified_at_commit.description: FULL 40-hex, never abbreviated. ⛔ A SHORT HASH IS NOT AN IDENTITY: the prior revision accepted 7 characters, so a nonexistent prefix validated and a real one could become ambiguous as the repo grows. EXISTENCE IS NOT CHECKABLE BY A SCHEMA and is enforced at load: `git cat-file -e <commit>^{commit}`.

candidate_set_digest.description: ⛔ BINDS THE RATIFICATION TO THE CANDIDATE SET IT ACTUALLY SAW. sha256 over the sorted `path\u0000git_blob_id` lines of every candidate `discovery_globs` matched at ratification. Without it `ratified_at_commit` names a moment and says NOTHING about what was in front of the ratifier -- two different candidate sets at one commit are indistinguishable, and 'ratified at HEAD' would be true of both.

discovery_globs.description: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY, AND THE SOLE SOURCE FOR REPORTING. A consumer may use these to REPORT candidates that are not admitted; it may never admit anything because a glob matched, and EDITING THEM CHANGES NO ADMISSION AND NO DIGEST. ⛔ THE PRIOR REVISION CARRIED THIS FIELD WHILE THE COMPILER READ ITS OWN CONSTANT -- so the field was INERT and a reader would have believed editing it changed the diagnostic. The compiler now reads only this one.

extension_population.description: The cards feeding the EXISTING W3 map/enrich path, and nothing else. Membership here says NOTHING about receiver-source eligibility -- those are independent consumer dimensions and one card may lawfully sit in both.

members.description: EXACT membership. An empty array is the claim 'nothing is admitted here', which a consumer can branch on.

receiver_source_populations.description: THREE INDEPENDENT POPULATIONS, one per receiver, keyed separately. ⛔ NOT one role enum: 4.0.0_SA_CRO~A withdrew that and the reason is load-bearing -- extension participation and receiver-source participation are INDEPENDENT CONSUMER DIMENSIONS, and a single role field makes the lawful overlap case unrepresentable.

ratified_discovery_globs.description: FROZEN. The globs `candidate_set_digest` was computed over, and the ONLY ones that digest speaks about. ⛔ SPLIT FROM `discovery_globs` BECAUSE THEY ARE TWO AXES AND ONE FIELD MADE THE OTHER UNUSABLE: with a single field, widening the diagnostic changed the digest input and the compiler REFUSED TO ADMIT -- so a purely diagnostic act broke admission, and the control that widens the glob could not run at all. The ratification ground is frozen; the lens over it is free.

x-rule24.axis: the candidate ground the ratification was taken over
x-rule24.intent: one -- what the digest covers; NOT what a reader may look at
x-rule24.mece: a glob is in the ratified ground or it is not
x-rule24.state_coherence: re-ratifying moves this and candidate_set_digest together; editing discovery_globs moves NEITHER.

git_blob_id.description: ⛔ THE GIT BLOB ID, NOT A DIGEST OF THE WORKING-TREE BYTES. The prior revision pinned sha256 of the bytes on disk and 9 of 13 members failed against Git-object bytes -- the CRLF/LF boundary, on a Windows checkout, in the field whose entire job is identity. A digest without its normalisation is not an identity. This value is produced and re-checked by `git hash-object`, so the SAME filters apply on both sides and the comparison cannot straddle the boundary.

repo_relative_path.description: Forward slashes only, no leading separator, no dot segments, no doubled separators, no drive letter, NO BACKSLASH ANYWHERE, no whitespace. ⛔ THE BACKSLASH CLAUSE IS NOT COSMETIC: on Windows `a\..\..\x` traverses and `\\host\share` is a UNC alias for a path outside the repo, and the prior pattern admitted both because it only forbade FORWARD-slash dot segments. A REGEX CANNOT RESOLVE A PATH, so containment inside the workspace is enforced at load, not here, and that split is stated rather than assumed.

subject_id.description: The card's own subject.id, PINNED HERE TOO. Path and blob identify the FILE; this identifies WHAT IT IS ABOUT, and a card whose subject was replaced under an unchanged path is caught by a content pin only because the bytes happened to move with it.

receiver_population.description: ⛔ FOUR INDEPENDENT AXES, NOT ONE FREE-TEXT BLOCK. The prior revision put the admission predicate, the census, the contract gap and the transform lifecycle in a single prose string, so no consumer could branch on any of them and no two could move separately -- Rule 24 (iii) inside the artifact that exists to govern admission.

members.description: Cards admitted as a source for THIS receiver. EMPTY IN v1 FOR ALL THREE, and the v1 clause below makes non-empty INEXPRESSIBLE rather than merely discouraged.

x-enum-definitions.absent: No card-to-L0 transform exists for this receiver, in any form.
x-enum-definitions.specified: A transform is specified and pinned but not implemented; still cannot admit.
x-enum-definitions.implemented: A transform exists and is pinned by transform_reference; admission is possible.

x-rule24.axis: the LIFECYCLE STATE of this receiver's transform
x-rule24.intent: one -- how far the transform has got; NOT which transform (transform_reference), NOT what a card must satisfy (admission_predicate), NOT why the population is empty (blocking_layers)
x-rule24.state_coherence: implementing a transform moves this and sets transform_reference; it moves NOTHING in admission_predicate or source_gap.

transform_reference.description: The exact transform, as `<repo-relative-path>@<40-hex commit>`, or null. SEPARATE FROM transform_status because a status is a lifecycle claim and a reference is an identity claim: the prior single `transform_version` string conflated them and accepted an arbitrary `v7` that named nothing.

admission_predicate.description: What a card must satisfy to be admitted here, STRUCTURED so a consumer can evaluate it rather than read it.

required_fields.description: Dotted paths inside the card that must be present.

basis_allowed.description: `absent` is excluded by construction: a receiver source with basis=absent asserts nothing.

blocking_layers.description: WHY this population is empty, as a SET of independent layers -- the census axis. An empty array means nothing blocks it.

x-rule24.intent: one -- the blockage census; NOT the remedy, NOT the lifecycle
x-rule24.mece: source (no payload exists anywhere) | registry (payloads exist, unadmitted) | transform (no governed projection) | compiler (no code path assigns declared). A layer is present or it is not.
x-rule24.state_coherence: closing one layer removes exactly that member and moves nothing else; the population becomes admissible only when the array is empty.

source_gap.description: The CONTRACT-LEVEL absence, separate from the census. A gap here cannot be closed by carding, globbing or transforming -- only by changing a contract.

x-enum-definitions.none: The card contract can express this receiver's payload.
x-enum-definitions.no_field_in_card_contract: SUBSTRATE_CARD.v2 has no field carrying the value at all.
x-enum-definitions.no_authored_projection: The field could exist but no card in the estate authors one.

allOf.$comment: implemented REQUIRES a reference: a lifecycle claim with nothing to point at is the unenforced-field defect.
no implemented transform => no members. A member admitted without a governed projection is a value with no provenance.

one_line_text.description: One line. Every terminator class is named EXPLICITLY -- CR, LF, U+2028, U+2029, NEL, vertical tab, form feed -- because `minLength` and a not-all-blank negative say nothing about line count, and 'one line' enforced by hope is how the shared contract shipped seven multi-line values.

v1_empty_receiver.description: v1 ONLY. Makes a non-empty receiver population INEXPRESSIBLE rather than discouraged. The prior revision described them as empty-by-contract in prose, and a phantom member, a duplicate, a conflicting overlap and an arbitrary transform version all validated cleanly -- a described constraint is not a constraint. When a governed transform exists, the registry moves to v2 and this clause stops binding by construction rather than by someone remembering to delete it.

allOf.$comment: ⛔ v1 MAKES A NON-EMPTY RECEIVER POPULATION INEXPRESSIBLE. The prior revision merely described them as empty-by-contract, and a phantom member, a duplicate, or an arbitrary transform version all validated cleanly. A described constraint is not a constraint.
